q: AI's first draft of your proposal is too long and sounds robotic. What does the lesson recommend?
options: Ask for a complete rewrite from scratch
Accept the draft — AI writes well enough
Tell AI to 'make it better' and wait
Give specific instructions, like cutting it by 20%, and an example of your voice, in rounds
explanation: Small, specific instructions beat vague ones: 'shorten by 20%' works, 'make it better' doesn't. If the voice is off, give it an example — 'here's how I'd say it — match this' — and steer it through two or three rounds.

q: Why does the lesson describe AI's draft as a 'working document' rather than a finished answer?
options: Because it is saved in the cloud
Because you build it in rounds — outline, rough draft, tighten, polish — in one place
Because only Claude can edit it
Because it is not suitable for real work
explanation: The working-document method improves the draft in place across rounds, so there's never a version-control mess. Each round you read, mark what's wrong and send it back with specific instructions.

q: Your organisation has firm tone rules — for example, 'we say customers, never clients'. How do you make every draft obey them?
options: Remind AI of the rules at the start of every chat
Fix the wording by hand after each draft
Paste your style rules once, covering vocabulary, voice, conventions and tone
Ask AI to write in a neutral tone instead
explanation: Paste your style guide in once and every draft obeys it — vocabulary, voice, conventions and tone. Organisations spend fortunes on brand voice; you can enforce yours with one paragraph of instructions.
